overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated videos demonstrates that first-person high-stakes planetary exploration ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme cosmic anomalies are FACTVERSE's primary growth drivers, frequently surpassing 800-1,000+ views and 20-38 likes. Conversely, brain psychology and repeated exact-title re-uploads underperform severely (often under 50 views and near-zero likes). 19-21 second pacing currently yields the highest retention and interaction metrics.

winning_patterns.pattern: 'What If You Fell Into...' immersive physical simulation hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views, 15 likes) dramatically outpace standard factual titles.
winning_patterns.action: Use visceral second-person sensory hooks placing the viewer directly inside extreme astronomical or planetary environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice...' (1,057 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,030 views), and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views) are top lifetime and recent performers.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight single mind-bending physical contradictions (e.g., solid matter acting bizarrely, extreme gravity, time/atomic destruction).

weak_patterns.pattern: Generic psychology and memory trivia hooks
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' achieved between 5 and 53 views across multiple uploads; song earworm titles hovered between 17 and 71 views.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize low-tension neuro-psychology trivia unless framed through high-stakes micro-drama or survival scenarios.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated uploads of 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' and 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' flatlined or stagnated with 0 comments.
weak_patterns.action: Strictly prohibit re-uploading identical hooks; explore brand new entities and phenomena rather than recycling asset concepts.

next_video.concept: What would happen to the human body when approaching a Magnetar
next_video.opening_direction: Immediate visual dive toward a hyper-magnetic dead star: 'If you stepped within a thousand kilometers of a magnetar, you wouldn't just die—your chemistry would cease to exist.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the magnetic field is so violently intense it pulls the electron clouds of your atoms into needle-thin shapes, disintegrating DNA and biomolecules instantly into pure radiation.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven 'What If You Fell/Approached' formula that drove over 1,000 views on prior planetary videos, while introducing an entirely novel, ultra-extreme space entity.
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not mention exoplanets already used (Gliese 436b, TrES-2b, 55 Cancri e, WASP-76b, HD 189733b, J1407b).
Avoid repeating diamond rain, molten glass, or burning ice tropes.
Focus on the unique atomic-level physics of magnetars.

experiment: Test whether lethal physics surrounding stellar remnants (magnetars/neutron stars) can match or beat exoplanet immersion videos in like-per-view ratio and comment discussion.
